candidate=r'''# Research candidate 354377 — ordinary refutation; zero credit

This is a complete ordinary counterexample to the literal MathDB statement and arXiv:2204.11084v1 Conjecture 6.2, not a formal certificate or acceptance recommendation. Novelty, significance and publication-version fidelity remain HOLD. No Pi task was run.

The source defines a finite set M as basic when every real-valued function on M is a sum of three functions of the separate coordinates. A layer is a coordinate hyperplane. An integer annihilation function has sum zero on each layer. Irreducible means that its integer values have gcd 1, not that all coefficients have the same sign. Minimal non-basic means non-basic with every proper subset basic. The source's Lemmas 1.5–1.6, their §2 linear-equation proofs, §5 primitive normalization and Conjecture 6.2 were read. The argument below supplies its own basic/minimality bridge.

Put n=3 and use these eight distinct points:

A=(2,2,2), B=(2,1,1), C=(1,2,1), D=(1,1,2),
E=(3,3,3), F=(3,1,1), G=(1,3,1), H=(1,1,3).

Give them coefficients (A,B,C,D,E,F,G,H)=(1,-1,-1,-1,-1,1,1,1).
All coordinates lie in {1,2,3}. For x=2, y=2, z=2 the layer pairs are respectively {A,B}, {A,C}, {A,D}; their sums are zero. For x=3, y=3, z=3 the layer pairs are {E,F}, {E,G}, {E,H}; their sums are zero. For x=1 the layer is {C,D,G,H}, for y=1 it is {B,D,F,H}, and for z=1 it is {B,C,F,G}. Each has two coefficients -1 and two +1. These are all nine layers, and all are nonempty. Thus this is an annihilation function with full support and gcd 1.

For completeness, every real annihilation vector is a multiple of this vector. Let its values at A and E be a and e. The six two-point layers force the values at B,C,D to be -a and those at F,G,H to be -e. The x=1 layer then gives -2a-2e=0, so e=-a. The other two layers impose no new restriction. Hence the kernel is exactly the line spanned by the displayed full-support vector. In particular every primitive integer annihilation vector is this vector or its negative: its value a at A is an integer, and the gcd of all eight values is |a|.

Here is the full minimal-non-basic bridge. Let L:R^9 -> R^M send nine layer weights to their sum at each point. A linear functional on R^M with coefficient vector v kills im L exactly when the layer sums of v vanish. If M were basic, L would be onto; a nonzero functional could not kill its image. Our vector is nonzero and kills im L, so M is not basic. More explicitly, the indicator of A has pairing 1 with our vector and therefore cannot be in im L.

For any proper subset K of M, a real annihilation vector on K extends by zero to an annihilation vector on M. The extended vector has a zero coordinate; the kernel characterization and the nonzero value of each of the eight displayed coefficients force its scalar a to be zero. Thus no nonzero functional on R^K kills the image of the corresponding layer-sum map. That map is onto: if its image were a proper subspace, extend a basis of the image to a basis of R^K and define a nonzero functional to vanish on the first basis and take value 1 on one added vector. This contradicts the absence of an annihilator. Hence every real function on K has coordinate-weight representation. Extend the three coordinate functions from {1,2,3} to R arbitrarily. Thus every proper subset is basic, as required, including the empty subset.

Finally sum |f|=8, whereas 2(|M|-n)=2(8-3)=10. Therefore the conjectured equality fails. This is a counterexample to a universal equality with all its witness conditions paid; it is not a finite verification offered as a universal proof. No enumeration, linear algebra program or numerical calculation was used.
